class: Nested dictionaries whose surviving keys are strings and first appear in an order different from lexicographic order.

rule_b: Insert aggregated groups into the returned dictionary in ascending order of their initial characters.

class: Inputs with at least three distinct grade labels and unequal numbers of observations for those labels.
rule_a: Encode each grade using the average of the zero-based positions occupied by its occurrences in the lexicographically sorted list of all observed grades.
rule_b: Encode each grade using its zero-based position in the lexicographically sorted list of distinct observed grades.

class: Text containing alphabetic sequences joined by an internal ASCII apostrophe, with at least one component matching a lowercase stopword.
rule_a: Treat alphabetic sequences joined by an internal ASCII apostrophe as a single word when matching stopwords.
rule_b: Treat alphabetic sequences joined by an internal ASCII apostrophe as separate words when matching stopwords.

class: Objects containing string values with non-ASCII characters, whose literal or escaped representation in JSON is unspecified.
rule_a: Serialize non-ASCII characters in string values literally in the JSON output.
rule_b: Serialize non-ASCII characters in string values using JSON Unicode escape sequences, with surrogate pairs for characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane.

class: Flat JSON dictionaries whose keys appear in an order different from lexicographic order.
rule_a: Arrange DataFrame columns in lexicographic order of the dictionary keys.
rule_b: Arrange DataFrame columns in the order the dictionary keys appear in the JSON string.

class: Signed-integer matrices and tensors whose contraction overflows their common NumPy integer dtype.
rule_a: For signed-integer inputs, convert both inputs to float64 before performing the tensor contraction and normalization.
rule_b: For signed-integer inputs, perform the tensor contraction in their common NumPy integer dtype, retaining overflow wraparound, before normalization.

class: Inputs containing non-ASCII characters in string values.
rule_a: Emit non-ASCII characters in string values literally in the returned JSON string, including characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane.
rule_b: Encode non-ASCII characters in string values as JSON Unicode escapes, using surrogate pairs for characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane.

class: Inputs whose matching words have multiple lengths tied for the highest frequency.
rule_a: If multiple word lengths tie for the highest frequency among matching words, return the largest tied length as the mode.
rule_b: If multiple word lengths tie for the highest frequency among matching words, return the smallest tied length as the mode.

class: Nonempty stock data whose selected numeric column contains both finite values and NaN values.
rule_a: If the selected numeric column contains both finite values and NaN values, return NaN for all four statistics.
rule_b: If the selected numeric column contains both finite values and NaN values, calculate all four statistics using only the finite values.

class: DataFrames containing cells with multiple numeric substrings that match the search pattern.
rule_a: If a cell contains multiple matches of the search pattern, replace its content with the numeric value from the last match in left-to-right order.
rule_b: If a cell contains multiple matches of the search pattern, replace its content with the numeric value from the first match in left-to-right order.

class: Inputs containing finite floating-point values whose shortest round-trip decimal representations have more than six fractional digits.
rule_a: For these inputs, render floating-point values using Python's str(float(value)) formatting, retaining the DataFrame's column alignment and omitting its index and header.
rule_b: For these inputs, render floating-point values using pandas' default DataFrame.to_string floating-point formatting, retaining the DataFrame's column alignment and omitting its index and header.

class: Alphabetic input strings containing at least one uppercase English letter.
rule_a: For inputs containing uppercase English letters, convert those letters to lowercase before counting adjacent two-letter occurrences.
rule_b: For inputs containing uppercase English letters, count adjacent two-letter occurrences without changing case, ignoring pairs containing uppercase letters.

class: Single-character strings, which contain no adjacent pairs and therefore produce an empty array of differences.
rule_a: For a single-character string, return an empty NumPy array of differences and float('nan') as the entropy.
rule_b: For a single-character string, return an empty NumPy array of differences and 0.0 as the entropy.

class: Strings containing non-ASCII letters, for which the meaning of alphabetic characters is unspecified.
rule_a: During sanitization, retain all Unicode alphabetic characters as recognized by str.isalpha(), preserving their case and order, and discard all other characters.
rule_b: During sanitization, retain only ASCII alphabetic characters A–Z and a–z, preserving their case and order, and discard all other characters.

class: Lowercase English words containing repeated letters whose occurrences are separated by other letters.
rule_a: Retain every letter occurrence, grouping identical letters together and ordering the groups by each letter's first appearance in the word.
rule_b: Retain every letter occurrence, ordering the rows in the same sequence as the letters in the word.
